name: Runner Extras - Object System Table
brief: Issue #2774: Object (2000000001) is the legacy application-database object registry, not a virtual table. The runner has no application database, so it projects its own object inventory - the one AllObj is answered from - into Object's column shape, and leaves the columns it has no source for at BC's own default. This suite pins the projection and the blanks so neither can change silently.
description: What Object CONTAINS is plain BC behaviour and BELONGS upstream. It is not service-tier-adjudicated YET, but the blocker this description used to cite is gone and saying so is the point of issue #3071. Both closures apply to a CLOUD-target app only: `Record "Object"` does not compile there (AL0296, the table is Scope = OnPrem), and the RecordRef route is refused at runtime by NavRecordRef.CheckIsOpenAllowed because 2000000001 is in SystemTables.InternalTables. NavRecordRef.IsOpenAllowed short-circuits on IsOnPremTarget() before that membership test, so a Target = OnPrem app is refused neither - and corpus PR StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#179 added exactly such an app. Corpus PR #197 now asks a real tier what rows this table holds, on the eight OnPrem legs; #3071 tracks reconciling the runner with the answer. The Cloud-target refusal itself was originally measured on the SIBLING id 2000000071 (corpus PR #153, withdrawn after all 8 BC legs of run 33968379281 refused it), with 2000000001 following by membership in the same FrozenSet rather than by its own measurement; AlRunner.Tests/RecordRefCompilationTargetScopeTests now executes BC's own CheckIsOpenAllowed body against 2000000001 directly, in both target directions, so that inference is retired. This suite therefore pins what the RUNNER does, which is what a runner suite is for: that rows appear at all with no application database behind them, that Type is a real part of the key rather than one ordinal for everything, that Object and AllObj cannot disagree about which objects exist because both are projected from the one inventory, that an object kind Object's own Type option cannot name gets no row rather than an invented ordinal, and that the columns with no runner source read blank rather than carrying a fabricated payload. The blanks are a DECLARED divergence, recorded in docs/limitations.md; issue #2771 tracks making such columns refuse by name instead. Target is OnPrem, not Cloud, for the AL0296 reason above.
